items.title: 67246_Buck Clayton oral history interview
items.q: There is some fans here like Jim Dunn in Connecticut, all of the Duke fans but over there everybody is that way

ctx.x: Well, you've probably had more experience in Europe than most American musicians who've been over there because I mean you lived there a long time. Did you find a short of big difference in the audiences as compared with those here?

Oh yes. All the difference in the world. You know there is, there is fans here that are just as great to you I think. Now you take the Duke Ellington fan club, you know that club, they're all dedicated fans, especially of Duke's. But it seems to me that all the people over there are that way, not just a few. There is some fans here like Jim Dunn in Connecticut, all of the Duke fans but over there everybody is that way, you know? And they just appreciate you so much. They give you so much more applause, that you…
you can't speak to them after they've been to Europe. They come back here and they want to be treated like they are over there and they don't.
